title: Resumable SSE segmenter and atomic emit proxy to prevent mid-JSON delimiter splits
author: Aisha Banerjee
description:
Motivation: Intermittent customer reports and stress test runs revealed cases where SSE chunk boundaries split JSON tokens and OpenAI-compatible function-call sentinels. This led to partial JSON messages being emitted to clients and, in some cases, tool/function-call ordering inversion at the client surface. The failure mode is most common under TCP segmentation and aggressive proxy buffering.

Goals: (1) Make SSE emission resumable and idempotent so clients can reconnect and continue without losing or duplicating mid-JSON fragments. (2) Ensure a small, deterministic set of rules that guarantee no delimiter escapes or function-call sentinel bytes are emitted across chunk boundaries. (3) Provide observability and opt-in feature flags to ship safely.

What this PR does: Introduces a new SSESegmenter component that buffers up to SSE_RESUME_WINDOW_BYTES (default 4096) and emits only whole JSON spans or safe prefixes; it also annotates fragments with a Replay-Id header to support idempotent resume. Adds an AtomicEmitProxy layer that serializes function-call sentinel handoffs so tool/function call boundaries are never split across writes. Adds a lightweight on-wire resume handshake (Replay-Id + last-offset) implemented in the OpenAI-compat proxy to remain backwards compatible with clients that do not opt in.

Key behaviors: - Segmenter guarantees any emitted chunk is "delimiter-safe": the last 8 bytes are scanned for potential JSON sentinel splits and, if ambiguous, the segmenter extends or trims to preserve UTF-8 and JSON token boundaries. - Replay-Id is deterministic per-stream and monotonic per session; the server will accept a resume request that provides the last-seen Replay-Id and offset if the server still has the window buffer cached. - AtomicEmitProxy serializes fn-call sentinel emission so function call start/end tokens are not interleaved with other event types. - Backpressure: when downstream is slow we hold up to SSE_SEGMENTER_WINDOW_MS (default 50ms) before forcing a safe flush; this prevents unbounded buffering while maintaining delimiter safety.

Testing and validation: - Unit tests for segmenter state machine covering UTF-8 boundaries, trailing-escape scenarios, and tiny-chunk splits. - Integration tests simulate split TCP frames and HTTP/1.1 chunking to reproduce earlier failures. - E2E test harness creates an OpenAI-compat client and verifies function-call ordering and structured JSON integrity across reconnects. Added CI job matrix entry to run the e2e simulator under higher packet fragmentation rates.

Rollout plan: Feature is gated behind SSE_SEGMENTER_ENABLED=false by default. We will enable for internal traffic for 48h and then progressively route low-risk orgs. Metrics added to monitor adoption and error surface. In the event of regressions the gate can be toggled off without restart.

Checklist:
- [x] Add SSESegmenter and AtomicEmitProxy implementation
- [x] OpenAI-compat proxy handshake implementation
- [x] Unit and integration tests
- [x] New metrics and dashboard entries
- [x] Feature flag and runtime config knobs

Related: ENG-7843 (streaming reliability), SUP-2101 (customer incident reproduced), ENG-7921 (fn-call ordering spec).

Author Aisha (2026-02-23): Reworked proxy to use lock-free ring buffer with token-bucket admission. Microbenchmarks attached to the PR comments. No measurable latency increase in median path.

release_notes: Fixes SSE streaming cases where TCP/HTTP chunking could split JSON tokens or OpenAI function-call sentinels. Introduces a resumable segmenter and atomic emitter that prevent partial JSON emits and preserve function-call ordering. Feature gated by SSE_SEGMENTER_ENABLED.
notes_for_ops: New runtime flags: SSE_SEGMENTER_ENABLED (bool), SSE_RESUME_WINDOW_BYTES (int, default 4096), SSE_SEGMENTER_WINDOW_MS (int, default 50). New metrics: sse.segment.repaired, sse.resume.attempts, sse.resume.failures, sse.delimiter.mismatch. Dashboards updated under Streaming -> Chunking Stabilization.
